 Kumar Kushagra joins India T20I squad as Kishan’s cover: Where does that leave Vaibhav Sooryavanshi? 
 Kumar Kushagra joins India’s squad as cover for injured Ishan Kishan ahead of the second T20I against New Zealand, while Vaibhav Sooryavanshi remains in contention.
 Neha Buswal | New Delhi | October 23, 2026 11:13 pm 
 15 April 2020 
 8 mins read -->
 -->
 -->
 Kumar Kushagra joins India T20I squad as Kishan’s cover: Where does that leave Vaibhav Sooryavanshi? (PC: IANS) 
 India have added wicketkeeper-batter Kumar Kushagra to their squad for the second T20I against New Zealand as cover for the injured Ishan Kishan, leaving the team management with decisions to make over its batting combination ahead of Saturday’s match in Christchurch.
 Kushagra, who is currently with the India A squad in Christchurch, has been called up by the Men’s Selection Committee, BCCI Honorary Secretary Devajit Saikia confirmed this in a release on Friday.
 Advertisement
 Kishan has been ruled out of the second T20I after sustaining a low-grade right adductor strain during the series opener. The BCCI Medical Team will continue to monitor his recovery.
 Advertisement 
 “Ishan Kishan is ruled out of the second T20I against New Zealand due to a low-grade right adductor strain, which he sustained during the first T20I of the series. The BCCI Medical Team is monitoring his progress,” the BCCI said in a statement.

 Sooryavanshi’s opportunity hinges on India’s team combination
 Kishan’s absence brings Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s prospects into focus as India consider their options for the second match. The 15-year-old is part of the squad, but whether he gets a place in the playing XI will depend on the balance the team management wants to strike.
 Sooryavanshi has had limited opportunities to feature, with Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma occupying the opening positions in the first T20I. A place in the top order would offer the teenager a chance to bring his attacking approach to the international stage, but India must also settle on the wicketkeeping arrangement and the overall composition of their XI.
 Kushagra’s addition gives the team another specialist wicketkeeper to consider. The selection decision, therefore, is not simply about replacing an unavailable player, but about which combination best suits India for the second game.
 What Sitanshu Kotak said about Sooryavanshi
 India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak had identified Sooryavanshi as a strong contender to come into the side if Kishan was unavailable. He also explained that Kishan’s fitness had influenced India’s batting order in the series opener, when Tilak Varma batted at No. 3 and Kishan came in at No. 5.
 “There was a lot of speculation I have also seen; just because Ishan had a strain in his groin, the batting order was changed,” Kotak told reporters.
 On the teenager’s chances, Kotak said the medical team’s assessment of Kishan would be a factor in the selection call.
 “If Ishan doesn’t play, unless he recovers completely, which the medical team will advise, Vaibhav (Sooryavanshi) could definitely step in for him. He is one of the strongest contenders,” he added.
 Sooryavanshi, who featured in the semi-final and final of India’s gold-medal-winning campaign at the Asian Games in Japan, is now among the options India can consider as they finalise their combination for the second T20I.
 India won the series opener by four wickets after chasing down 226 in Christchurch. The second T20I will be played at the same venue on Saturday, before the teams travel to Wellington, Auckland and Hamilton for the final three matches on October 27, 30 and November 1.
 India’s updated squad for the second T20I
 Shreyas Iyer (captain), Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson (wicketkeeper), Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Tilak Varma (vice-captain), Axar Patel, Shivam Dube, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Naman Dhir, Prince Yadav, Mayank Yadav, Arshdeep Singh, Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Varun Chakaravarthy, Kuldeep Yadav and Kumar Kushagra (wicketkeeper).
